recentItems.title: ‘F**k Flock’: Is the backlash to surveillance cameras winning?
recentItems.description:
Flock cameras have sparked a nationwide debate over privacy and public safety, as law enforcement says the technology is an invaluable tool while critics argue the surveillance violates their privacy. CNN’s Meena Duerson visits a city where all the Flock cameras were destroyed, and sits down with masked activist NoMark to understand what’s behind the growing backlash.

recentItems.title: ‘Heartbreaking’ devastation in Nepal now worsened by rain
recentItems.description: Rain is now coming for the flood-affected areas in Nepal. Authorities fear this could cause further devastation, potentially secondary flooding and may hamper rescue efforts. CNN's Hanako Montgomery shows the damage done to Dhunge Bazaar, close to Trishuli River. #CNN #News #Nepal

recentItems.title: Son of US couple who narrowly escaped Nepal flood: 'Grateful for the miracle'
recentItems.description: The son of an American couple who survived the devastating floods in Nepal is preparing to reunite with his parents. Looking ahead to the reunion, his mother told CNN, "I'm going to hug them and cry because I am an emotional mama." Her son, Vikram Ravi, reflected on the harrowing ordeal, telling Brianna Keilar, "I'm just thankful that I was able to hear her tell me that she's okay, rather than having to go look for her."

recentItems.title: Two lakes threaten Nepal after deadly flood in 'hazard-prone' region
recentItems.description:
Perilous rescue efforts along the China-Nepal border are being complicated by the risk of new flooding or landslides, with authorities in China and Nepal briefly pausing rescue operations Friday due to those fears.

A barrier lake – holding enough water to fill an estimated 1,000 Olympic swimming pools – began overflowing on the China-Nepal border, where it formed after a powerful landslide and torrential flooding devastated the area on Wednesday. A barrier lake is a body of water created by debris damming up a river.

0:00 The two new barrier lakes threatening rescuers' lives
2:29 Scientists explain what happened
3:36 One of the most 'hazard-prone landscapes' on the planet

recentItems.title: ICE detains asylum seeker while boarding plane
recentItems.description: Indi Veitia is an asylum seeker from Venezuela who was arrested by ICE at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport. CNN's Shimon Prokupecz spoke with Veitia after she was recently released from an ICE detention facility in Georgia.

recentItems.title: ICE detains right-wing provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos
recentItems.description: Controversial British figure Milo Yiannopoulos, who gained a reputation as a right-wing provocateur more than a decade ago, has been detained by ICE at a Louisiana airport, the Department of Homeland Security said.

recentItems.title: Did the Meta settlement go far enough?
recentItems.description:
CNN spoke with three mothers who say social media played a role in their children’s deaths about Meta’s $18 billion settlement of a multistate lawsuit alleging the company intentionally designed addictive platforms that harmed young people’s mental health. 

As part of the settlement with states, Meta agreed to make sweeping changes to Facebook and Instagram and let an independent auditor evaluate how it’s implementing those changes. CNN’s Clare Duffy reports.

recentItems.title: Trump admin pushing to trade Yosemite land to private developer
recentItems.description:
The Trump administration is considering trading a portion of Yosemite National Park to a private developer in exchange for land elsewhere in California. CNN examines what the developer stands to gain from the controversial swap, and our panel debates whether trading away protected federal land makes sense.
